en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on the Naked;
30. The Training Rule on the Suspension of the Kathina.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a certain lay follower had a monastery built for the Saṅgha.
He wished to give out-of-season robes to both Saṅghas at the dedication ceremony of that monastery.
At that time, however, the kaṭhina had been spread for both Saṅghas.
Then that lay follower approached the Saṅgha and requested the removal of the kaṭhina.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, having given a discourse on the Dhamma on this occasion and in this context, addressed the bhikkhus:
“I allow you, monks, to suspend the kaṭhina.
And thus, monks, should the kaṭhina be suspended:
An experienced and competent monk should inform the Saṅgha:”
‘Let the Saṅgha hear me, venerable sirs.
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha revoke the kaṭhina.
This is the motion.’
"Venerable sirs, let the Sangha hear me.
The Sangha is lifting the *kathina*.
Whoever among the venerable ones approves of the lifting of the *kathina*, let him remain silent."
"Whoever does not approve may speak.
The kaṭhina has been dismantled by the Saṅgha; it is approved by the Saṅgha, therefore there is silence. Thus do I understand this.
Then that lay follower approached the community of bhikkhunīs and requested the dismantling of the kaṭhina.
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā,
thinking, "There will be robe-cloth for us," postponed the dismantling of the kaṭhina.
Then that lay follower criticized, complained, and spread it about:
“How can it be that the bhikkhunīs will not grant us the ending of the kaṭhina?
The bhikkhunīs heard that lay follower complaining, grumbling, and expressing his indignation.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... [as above] ...they complained, grumbled, and expressed their indignation:
“How can the noble lady Thullanandā obstruct a legitimate dismantling of the kaṭhina?
… [as before] … “Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā obstructs a legitimate dismantling of the kaṭhina?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā obstruct a legitimate suspension of the kaṭhina?
This, bhikkhus, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of those with faith…” [and so on].
And furthermore, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule as follows:
“Whichever nun should obstruct a legitimate dismantling of the kaṭhina, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whichever nun” means:
Whichever [nun] of such a kind... "a nun" ...pe...
this is the nun intended in this context.
The "legitimate" (dhammika) suspension of the kaṭhina occurs when the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, being in concord, assembles and suspends it.
"Should obstruct" means...
If she objects, thinking, “How can this kaṭhina not be suspended? there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If it is legitimate and she objects while perceiving it as legitimate, there is an offense of expiation.
If it is legitimate and she objects while being doubtful of it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one perceives what is lawful as unlawful, there is no offense.
If one perceives what is unlawful as lawful, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one is doubtful regarding what is unlawful, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is contrary to the Dhamma, but she perceives it as contrary to the Dhamma,
there is no offense.
There is no offense if she prevents [the action] by pointing out the benefits.
"Against one who is insane," "against one who is a first-offender.
The tenth training rule is concluded.
The third chapter: The Chapter on the Naked Ascetics.
